To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) moment matching techniques are well suited for delay and transition-time estimation in the context of interconnect optimization; 2) the transition time constraints are as important as the delay constraints; 3) moment matching based techniques can be used to estimate transition times and delay times with high accuracy; 4) the transition time and the delay times can be optimized using dynamic programming; and 5) the dynamic programming algorithm is efficient.

(a) the delay and transition time constraints can be satisfied by a combination of driver sizing and repeater insertion; and (b) the delay and the transition time can be accurately estimated by moment-matching techniques.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of techniques for the accurate estimation of RC interconnect delays and transition times and the synthesis of RC interconnects which satisfy user specified delay and transition time requirements.
(1) accurate delay/transition time estimation for RC interconnect, (2) accurate repeater insertion and sizing, and (3) accurate driver sizing and wire sizing.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a new approach for interconnect optimization which is spec-based and employs accurate moment-matching delay and transition time estimation techniques and an accurate repeater delay model.
our approach yields delay and transition times estimates within 5-7% of circuit simulation, while Elmore delay techniques yield delay estimates within 20-30% of circuit simulation.
the delay and transition time estimation and optimization algorithms are based on a unified framework which is accurate, efficient, and scalable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Elmore delay and transition time model is not adequate for spec-based design.
the Elmore delay and transition time estimation techniques, while being computationally efficient, can be very misleading in terms of the accuracy of the results.
accurate moment-matching delay and transition time techniques are well suited for spec-based interconnect design.
